newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia natgas trade needs spot market - expert.
newsitem.headline: Australia natgas trade needs spot market - expert.

text.p: The deregulation of Australia's natural gas market is likely to lead to the development of a spot market in natural gas, an industry expert said on Wednesday.
"It is very hard to see open access markets developing in this country without spot markets behind them," Paul Breslin, a director of ACIL Economics, told a gas reform conference.

Australian state governments have pledged to open their respective markets to competition. A government-appointed committee is in the process of formulating a national access code which is expected to be legislated by June 1998.
Breslin said risk management in an open access regime was almost impossible without a spot market.
"The electricity market is unlikely to want to use a take or pay arangement to buy gas," he said.
Under a take or pay arrangement, the user pays for the gas irrespective of whether they use their complete quota.
Breslin said trading in a new spot gas market was likely to be low initially, but build up as new trading products were introduced.
If introduced, Australian spot natural gas prices were likely to remain steady up until about 2005 when new supplies would be required to meet demand, Breslin said.
He added that he believed the role of regulators in the formation of spot markets was primarily to define the property rights of tradeable contracts so as to facilitate trade.
"I believe there is no reason to regulate these markets and regulators should be looking for systems to avoid heavy-handed regulation,"he said.

A secondary market in pipeline capacity also had the potential to develop in Australia, Breslin said, adding that one of the biggest problems faced by the gas market was monopoly pipelines keeping potential suppliers out with high tariffs.
Breslin said a pipeline capacity market could alleviate this problem if gas buyers were also assigned property rights for the use of the pipeline.
Such rights could be traded on a secondary market.
